title: Quantum-enhanced single and multiparameter metrology in qutrit ensembles by generalized twisting dynamics
authors: Deep Datta, Sayam Chakraborty, John Drew Wilson, Vaibhav Madhok, Athreya Shankar
abstract: Quantum-enhanced sensing with atomic ensembles has predominantly focused on qubit-based protocols, despite the growing ability of many experimental platforms to coherently control and entangle multi-level systems. Here, we investigate quantum-enhanced sensing with qutrit ensembles by introducing three experimentally feasible qutrit generalisations of the one-axis twisting (OAT) model that involve entangling operations only between two levels, while the third level primarily acts as a spectator. We characterize the metrological utility of the dynamically generated states using the quantum Fisher information toolbox. We find numerically that all three models offer considerable freedom in encoding direction for quantum-enhanced sensing, with up to 6 out of 8 possible directions exhibit near-Heisenberg scaling after a short evolution time. We discuss experimental access to this enhanced metrological precision via effective time-reversal protocols. Furthermore, we examine the practical issues of estimation ambiguity and local dissipation, and show that they can be largely overcome by optimizing the sensor operating point. Finally, we show that the measurement incompatibility in estimating multiple parameters simultaneously encoded in different directions with near-Heisenberg scaling of precision is suppressed at the zero operating point as the system size increases. In the process, we find that one of the models enables near-Heisenberg scaling metrology with a pair of commuting generators, a possibility that arises from the $su(3)$ algebra and is thus absent in qubit-ensemble based sensors of collective $SU(2)$ rotations.
summary: This paper explores quantum sensing using three novel qutrit models derived from the OAT Hamiltonian. By analyzing the Quantum Fisher Information, the authors show these systems achieve near-Heisenberg scaling and, crucially, enable simultaneous, compatible estimation of multiple parameters—a feat difficult in qubit systems. This advances the field by demonstrating robust, high-precision sensing in multi-level atomic ensembles.
main_problem: Investigating quantum-enhanced single and multiparameter metrology using qutrit ensembles, moving beyond standard qubit protocols.
main_result: The proposed qutrit models achieve near-Heisenberg scaling for sensing and demonstrate a novel mechanism for compatible multiparameter estimation using commuting generators from the su(3) algebra.
method: The metrological utility is characterized using the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) toolbox, analyzing the scaling of the QFIM and the Uhlmann curvature.
model_or_system: The system involves N three-level atoms (qutrits) whose dynamics are governed by generalizations of the One-Axis Twisting (OAT) model, specifically QOAT, BOAT, and QXY Hamiltonians, operating within the su(3) algebra.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Uhlmann Curvature, and the scaling of incompatibility measures (R).
important_parameters: System size (N), evolution time ($t$), and the operating point of the sensor.
main_assumptions: The study addresses practical issues like local dissipation and estimation ambiguity by optimizing the sensor operating point.
figures_summary: Figure 9 illustrates the time evolution of eigenvalues and the Frobenius norm of the commutator for two generators in the BOAT model, showing compatibility.
paper_structure: The paper reviews metrology concepts, introduces and analyzes the three qutrit extensions (QOAT, BOAT, QXY) using QFI, discusses experimental protocols, and finally addresses practical limitations like dissipation and compatibility.
why_interesting: This work extends quantum sensing theory to multi-level systems (qutrits), providing concrete, experimentally feasible models that surpass the limitations of qubit-only approaches, particularly regarding multiparameter estimation compatibility.

FIG. 2. Contribution of the Gell-Mann operators in the opti- mal generator Gopt for (a) QOAT (N = 40), (b)BOAT(N = 40) and (c) QXY (N = 40). The vertical black dashed lines indicate the tpeak for each model. At tpeak, for the QOAT and QXY models, the optimal generator has no contribution from λ8. However, there is very little contribution from λ8 for the BOAT model.

FIG. 4. Scaling of eigenvalues of Σ matrix at tpeak with system size N for (a)QOAT, (b) BOAT and (c) QXY models. The solid lines are linear fits, and the markers are the plot points. The slope of the fit lines gives the exponent of N. QOAT has a 4 orthogonal generators for which sensitivity scales approx- imately as Heisenberg scaling (∝N 2), whereas BOAT and QXY have 6 such generators. The N 2 and N scaling lines are shown as dashed and dotted black lines, respectively, in each plot.

FIG. 5. Comparison of the classical Fisher information (CFI) obtained using the time-reversal (solid blue line) and identity (solid red line) protocols with the maximum quantum Fisher information, µmax(FQ) (blue dashed), for N = 10. Results are shown for (a) the QOAT model, (b) the BOAT model, and (c) the QXY model. The vertical black dashed line marks the tpeak for each model. The CFI obtained under the time- reversal protocol saturates the optimal QFI for all models, whereas under the identity protocol it does not. The same measurement basis also saturates the QFI corresponding to any other encoding direction.
